yaml.feature_when_absent: Measured, not summarised: every read of a YAML-only site dies loudly. load_site('.yaml' non-JSON) raises ValueError('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)') because _yaml_load_unique returns None and the json fallback cannot parse YAML, and load_registry over the shipped registry fails the same way before its schema check. '.json' sites are unaffected, and JSON-shaped '.yaml' sites still load with the identical value and identical duplicate-key rejection (a parser substitution, not a semantic one). Net: the lane policy cannot read its own registry at all - the failure is loud and total, never a quietly different document.

cryptography.feature_when_absent: Measured: fhs.issuer_binding.verify_signature raises IssuerBindingRefusal(code=WP-FHS-03.FIRST_FAIL:ISSUER_BINDING_INVALID, 'signature verification unavailable: ...') instead of returning a boolean, and bind() propagates that refusal at its first gate, so no permit is ever bound. native_admission.verify_signature raises InvariantViolation('ERR_NATIVE_CRYPTO_DEPENDENCY'). hg_kseos.user_trust does not import at all (ImportError at module level, no fallback). No path degrades toward 'verified': refusal is the only outcome.

yaml.why_not_silent_accept: no case ran without an exception and returned a different document than the dependency-present run
yaml.retired_phrase: fail-open is NOT the measured behaviour and must not be used for this module; the three load_site file classes resolve to three different outcomes

mode.issuer_binding: fail-closed typed refusal at call time (IssuerBindingRefusal)
mode.native_admission: fail-closed typed refusal at call time (InvariantViolation)

notes: _yaml_load_unique returns None both when PyYAML is absent and when the document's top-level value is legitimately null; load_site cannot tell the two apart, so a '.yaml' file whose content is 'null' takes the JSON fallback. Measured separately from dependency absence - it is a code-shape hazard, not a dependency hazard.

pip 25.0.1 accepts '.[yaml]' with no warning and no error even though no such extra is declared: the request silently resolves to the default install. Declaring the extra is therefore not optional if the docs promise it.
The three pyprojects disagree: HEAD requires cryptography>=42, r4 and main require nothing. The same module is a hard install requirement in one tree and an undeclared assumption in another.
